info.title: Tools — folio-assistant-sci
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Report which of the harness's optional and required dependencies are present on this machine, and what each unmet one blocks.

required_only.description: Report only the dependencies without which the harness cannot run.

report.description: Per-dependency: present, absent, or could not be determined.

post.description: Validate the block manifests under a path against their schemas.

targetPath.description: A paper or chapter directory; absent, every paper the folio declares.

issues.description: One line per issue, with its block and file. Exit 2 means NO FOLIO WAS FOUND — could-not-determine, never valid.

post.description: Drive a folio's built viewer in headless Chromium and report the blocks whose diagrams, SVGs, LaTeX math or markdown do not render — with `--screenshot` to save the pictures.

screenshot.description: Save the screenshots as well as the verdict.

report.description: Per block: rendered, or the failure. Needs a FOLIO's `build/viewer/paper.json` and its `folio-assistant/ui`, so it exits 2 with `No paper.json found` in the platform (could-not-determine).

post.description: Compile a rendered paper's `main.tex` with latexmk inside a TeX Live (full) image, for a host with Docker but no TeX engine. The image carries TeX Live, latexmk, Pandoc, latexdiff, graphviz and poppler-utils; it does not run the content pipeline, which renders the chapters on the host first.

mainTex.description: The rendered paper's top-level `.tex`, relative to the checkout.

pdf.description: The compiled PDF beside the input.

x-selection.when: A step needs a compiled PDF, `pdflatex` is not on PATH, and Docker is available — the container alternative to `tex-install`.
x-selection.limits: Needs Docker. The first build pulls ubuntu:24.04 and texlive-full (several GB); later runs reuse the image.
x-selection.cost: One image build (10-20 minutes, once), then one latexmk compile per run.

post.description: Turn a pdflatex log's Overfull \hbox warnings into a located, actionable report, with a threshold so a long tail of trivial overruns does not bury the real ones.

max.description: Fail above this count, for use as a gate.

report.description: Located overfull boxes. Requires a build log: with no log there is nothing to read, which is could-not-determine rather than clean.

post.description: Lint TeX source for the pdflatex-compile failure classes a permissive AST parser accepts — the ones that pass validation and then break the build.

warn.description: Report without failing — for a corpus not yet clean.

findings.description: Compile-breaking hazards, located. A clean run here is not a successful compile; it is the absence of these classes.

post.description: Compile LaTeX source documents into PDF using latexmk with safe shell-escape isolation across CI events.

tex.description: The TeX source file to compile (e.g. main.tex).

args.description: Additional arguments to forward to latexmk.

pdf.description: The compiled PDF document. Exits 2 if the source file is missing (could-not-determine).

post.description: Inspect Lean declarations chapter by chapter for proofs that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and still carry no mathematical content — assuming what they claim, concluding something trivially true, or resting on a false premise.

chapter.description: One chapter instead of the whole corpus.

checkAxioms.description: Axiom-cleanliness is a separate question from vacuity: a proof can be axiom-clean and still assume its conclusion.

findings.description: Sorry inventory and trivial-truth detections. Sibling of `lean-coverage`, not an alternative to it: that one COUNTS what is proved, this one asks whether a proof says anything.

post.description: Build every Lean project in the workspace from the root Lake manifest, so cross-package dependencies resolve against it rather than a possibly-stale per-paper manifest. Writes a committable build-status sidecar every run.

paper.description: Build one paper instead of all of them.

cache.description: Fetch the Mathlib cache first. A from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes against ~2 for a restore.

logDir.description: Where logs and the status sidecar go.

status.description: `lean-build-status.json` — committable, so a green build is distinguishable from one nobody ran.

post.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt `.lake/` artefacts for a Lean package. Always try `restore` first: a from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes, a restore about two.

action.description: The verb. `doctor` tells a restore that silently missed from one that worked.

lakeRoot.description: The package whose `.lake/` is acted on.

result.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

post.description: Count how many provable blocks — theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary — carry a full Lean proof rather than a sorry, per paper. The completeness half of the Lean audit: what is formalised, and what is still a gap.

contentRoot.description: Where content blocks live. not a Lean project root.

coverage.description: Provable blocks, and how many are sorry-free. A count, not a verdict: a sorry-free proof can still be vacuous, which is the sibling node's question.

post.summary: Formal edges from the Lean build
post.description: Extract ELABORATED formal dependencies between a folio's lean.ref declarations (LeanArchitect's rule over the folio's own lean.ref set). Needs a Lean toolchain and a built Lake project. Tagged declarations missing from the build are reported, never recorded as dependency-free; with ingest the result is recorded in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

lake_dir.description: The folio's Lake project directory (holds lakefile.* and .lake/).

root.description: Content root to collect lean.ref targets from (default: the folio's declared one).

ingest.description: Record the result in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

report.description: The extracted edges, or why they could not be determined — never an empty edge set in place of a failure.

post.summary: Build a Lean package's HTML docs (doc-gen4)
post.description: Build the doc-gen4 HTML render of a folio's Lake package — the visualiser of a declared `lean` directory — with `lake -R -Kenv=dev build <Lib>:docs`, cache-aware: refuses while another lake/lean process holds `.lake/`, refuses on a restored tree that carries no traces (a Lake build there EVICTS the cache), checks or restores the warm cache first, and enables a sentinel-commented doc-gen4 `[[require]]` for this build only, restoring the lakefile on exit. Never runs `lake update`. Output: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`.

lakeRoot.description: The Lake package directory whose lakefile requires (or sentinel-comments) doc-gen4, e.g. `folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean`.

lib.description: The `lean_lib` to document, e.g. `QOU` (a Lean library name: alphanumerics, dot, underscore, hyphen). Repeat for several.

restore.description: Restore the warm cache first (about 2 minutes) instead of only checking it.

allowCold.description: Build without a warm cache: Mathlib from source, 30-60 minutes before doc-gen4 starts.

dryRun.description: Run every guard, print the build command, build nothing.

render.description: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`, doc-gen4's output, printed as the last line. Feed it to `lean-render-publish`.

x-selection.when: A folio's declared `lean` directory needs its visualiser (the doc-gen4 render) built or refreshed, before `lean-render-publish` wraps it.
x-selection.limits: doc-gen4 renders the WHOLE import closure, Mathlib included. It does not prune; prune at publish. Refuses, rather than risks, a shared or untraced `.lake/`. Never run it while another agent holds the folio's Lean cache.
x-selection.cost: Unmeasured. One doc-gen4 compile, then one doc pass per module of the closure — thousands for a Mathlib package; qou's July render was 4,193 pages, 545 MB. Needs that much free disk beyond the build.

post.summary: Publish the dynamic Lean viewer: doc-gen4 declaration data as knowledge-graph shards
post.description: Ingest doc-gen4's per-module declaration data (`.lake/build/doc-data/declaration-data-<Module>.bmp`) into JSON-LD shards — one per module, with declaration nodes, `imports` edges and `formalizes` edges to the content blocks whose `lean.ref` names each declaration — and publish them under the folio's site with a single viewer page that loads modules, signature chunks and the search list on demand. Signatures are chunked 500 declarations per file so a 12,804-declaration module stays usable. With `--base` it writes a STAGING overlay: only modules whose content hash differs from the published base, plus `overlay.json`; the viewer loads the rest from the base. Rails the viewer page with the same pass as `lean-render-publish`.

module.description: A module root to keep (`qou` keeps `QOU`). Repeat for several.

contentRoot.description: Content tree whose blocks' `lean.ref` become `formalizes` edges.

ref.description: Branch or sha for block links.

contentPrefix.description: Path of the content root inside the repo, for block links.

base.description: Published `data/` of the base graph; enables the STAGING overlay.

externalBase.description: Where links into pruned modules go. Default the community mathlib4 docs.

platform.description: The index checkout holding the rail pass.

noRail.description: Publish only; the caller rails the site.

viewer.description: `<site>/<route>/`: index.html, viewer.js/css, extracted signature styles, config.json and `data/` (index.json, names.json, m/<Module>.jsonld, m/<Module>.<k>.sig.json, overlay.json).

x-selection.when: Instead of `lean-render-publish` when the folio publishes its Lean as a dynamic viewer over graph shards, and for STAGING branches with `--base`.
x-selection.limits: doc-gen4 still has to elaborate: the shards come from its doc-data, so `lean-html-docs` (or a restored doc-gen4 cache) runs first. Links into pruned modules go to the community docs, built from their Mathlib. Docstrings are rendered client-side with marked and MathJax from CDNs.
x-selection.cost: Measured on qou 2026-10-11: 3,011 modules, 53,565 declarations, 651 formalizing a block; 6,005 files / 171 MB / 13 s; a no-change overlay writes 0 module files.

post.summary: Publish a Lean render under a folio site, with the harness rail
post.description: Stage a doc-gen4 render under a folio's built site (`<site>/<route>/`, default `lean/`) and give every page the harness navbar and rail by running `cat-harness/scripts/rail-standalone-pages.ts --foreign-site` over the site — the same rail `stage-folio-local.ts` applies to the folio's own pages. Leaves out Lake's `.hash`/`.trace` bookkeeping, marks doc-gen4's iframe navbar and `find/` redirect `folio-navbar: none` so no rail is drawn inside the sidebar, adds a layout shim so the rail does not cover doc-gen4's fixed sidebar, and with `--modules` prunes to the folio's own modules, repointing links into dropped ones to the community docs. Then asserts every staged page is railed or declined.

site.description: The folio's built site (`_site` from build-folio-site.ts).

module.description: A Lake package whose module root to keep (`qou` keeps `QOU/`, matched case-insensitively). Repeat for several. Default: keep everything.

externalBase.description: Where links into pruned modules go. Default the community mathlib4 docs.

homeLabel.description: The rail's home row: the folio's instance name, e.g. `qou`.

instance.description: Rail as this instance's own site (its name, mark and graphs), as rail-standalone-pages.ts --instance.

platform.description: The index checkout holding the rail pass. Default `$FOLIO_ASSISTANT_ROOT`, then the nearest ancestor that has it.

noRail.description: Stage only; the caller rails the site itself.

pages.description: `<site>/<route>/`, railed, plus the rail's shared data under `<site>/assets/navbar/`.

x-selection.when: After the folio's site is built and before it is checked and published (`stage-folio-local.ts` step 2 runs the same rail): put the Lean render into it as the `lean` directory's visualiser.
x-selection.limits: Pruned links point at the community docs, built from THEIR Mathlib rather than the folio's pin; doc-gen4's search index still lists pruned declarations, whose hits 404. The rail's assets load from the platform's published site, as on every foreign-site page.
x-selection.cost: Measured on qou's July render: pruned to QOU,UGB,Fred2005 34 pages / 29 MB / about 5 s; unpruned 4,193 pages / 533 MB / 347 s.

post.description: Install the toolchain pinned in `lean-toolchain`, fetching it from the GitHub release rather than through elan's downloader. Idempotent, and it detects partial state rather than re-downloading.

toolchain.description: The linked toolchain name, and the per-repo override that selects it.

post.description: Quick preview of a paper folio's branch: render the paper with the sci print template (plus the folio's notation fragment when it has one), then compile ONLY the chapters changed against a base ref, and a colored and a plain latexdiff of each. A preview, never a publish build. Run from the folio.

base.description: The ref to diff against. Default `origin/main`.

chapters.description: Chapter slugs, comma-separated. Default: the chapters whose sources changed against `base`.

paper.description: The paper's slug. Default: the folio's only paper; with several, the tool refuses and names them.

out.description: Output directory, which the folio should gitignore. Default `build-feature`.

notation.description: The folio's notation fragment, appended after the template. Default `<paper dir>/latex/notation-preamble.tex` when present.

preload.description: Bun preload that configures the platform's injected registries (values, Lean packages). Default `scripts/preload-registry.ts` when present. It must import the same platform checkout as this tool.

preview.description: `<out>/changed.pdf`, `<out>/<chapter>.diff-color.pdf` and `.diff-plain.pdf`, with the logs and `<out>/build.log` beside them. The render also rewrites the folio's `chapters/` and `main.tex`.

x-selection.when: Iterating on a paper's prose or mathematics, before a full build: you want to see the changed chapters typeset, and what changed, in a minute or so instead of compiling the whole paper.
x-selection.limits: A preview: cross-references outside the build show '??', margin notes are off by default (`FAST_PREVIEW=1`, about 2x faster), and a chapter's base latexdiff degrades to 'all added' when the base ref has no committed chapter .tex. Needs pdflatex/latexmk for the PDFs and latexdiff for the diffs; without them only the render runs.
x-selection.cost: One paper render (about 20-40 s on a 2,900-block paper) plus one pdflatex compile per output PDF.

post.description: Render a paper's content objects to LaTeX chapters: load the paper manifest, resolve its chapters and blocks, render, validate the LaTeX AST, and write the chapter files. With no manifest it builds the folio's only paper, and refuses — naming them — when there are several or none.

paperManifest.description: The paper's `<paper>.ts` manifest; absent, the folio's single paper.

outDir.description: Where to write the chapters; absent, `chapters/` at the content root.

chapters.description: One `.tex` per chapter under the output directory.

post.description: Read, write or clear the stored rendering preferences — engine, format, scope, math renderer, print mode.
Open a rendered PDF, HTML page or image in the system browser, or list the renders available to open.

opened.description: What was opened, or the list of candidates.

post.description: Render the dependency graph of a paper's proof objects from `proof-objects.json` as SVG (or DOT), each node linking to its anchor in the published PDF.

pdfBaseUrl.description: The published PDF, for the anchor links.

dotOnly.description: Write DOT source instead of rendering.

post.description: Extract the theorem, lemma and definition environments of a paper's LaTeX chapters into `proof-objects.json` — the manifest the dependency graph and the proof-status update read.

manifest.description: proof-objects.json. A chapter file that is missing is skipped with a warning, not treated as empty.

post.summary: Proof status from a Lean build
post.description: Update each proof object's status in `proof-objects.json` from a Lean build log — which objects built, which carry `sorry`, which failed. Exits 1 on a manifest with no objects rather than writing an empty status.

buildLog.description: The Lean build log; stdin when absent.

manifest.description: proof-objects.json with statuses updated in place.

post.summary: Install TeX Live in a sandbox
post.description: Install TeX Live (full) and latexmk where no TeX engine is present, disabling the firewalled launchpad PPAs that otherwise abort `apt-get update`. Idempotent: does nothing when pdflatex and memoize.sty are already present. Run it in the background. pdflatex unpacks early but is not usable until the post-install format build ends (`kpsewhich memoize.sty` returning a path is the ready signal).

engine.description: A `pdflatex --version` line on success. The installed packages are system-wide.

x-selection.when: A step needs to compile TeX (`paper-feature-build`'s PDFs, a full paper build) and `pdflatex` is not on PATH.
x-selection.limits: Debian/Ubuntu with apt and sudo only. Installs system packages; it does not touch the repository.
x-selection.cost: About 5 GB of disk and 10-20 minutes, once per container.

post.description: Parse every `tex` snippet in a folio's blocks and report what will not compile — structural, not textual: it reads an AST rather than matching patterns. Complementary to `latex-preflight`, which gates a main.tex before a compile, and to `latex-overfull`, which reads a log after one.

paper.description: One folio by slug. Absent, every folio the content root holds.

file.description: A single `.md` block, for the narrow case.

compile.description: Also compile each snippet with pdflatex — needs a TeX distribution, which the base `requires` does NOT claim.

warningsLog.description: Write a QA-compatible log to this path.

report.description: Per snippet, what will not compile. With no folio to scan it reports `Files scanned: 0` and exits 2 (could-not-determine). Read the scanned count before reading the verdict.

post.description: Catch the source patterns that crash pdflatex but read as ordinary prose — a bare `_` or `^` in a bibliography field, `|` inside a markdown table cell where it is also the column separator, a `$…$` span across two lines, markdown link syntax inside a fenced tex block, a double subscript.

strict.description: Exit 1 on any finding, for use as a gate.

report.description: Hazards with file and line, plus a committed sidecar. Run where no folio exists it says `No .md files found … refusing to report success. This audits a FOLIO's content; folio-assistant is the platform.` and exits 2 (could-not-determine).

Dpi.description: Dots per inch for rendered formulae.

Flag.description: A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word

InstanceId.description: A workflow instance id — the stem of a file in the bean graph's workflow-state node

LakeCacheAction.description: A lake-cache verb: restore prebuilt oleans, seed them, or diagnose why a restore missed.

Markdown.description: Markdown text. Not admissible as a command-line argument — see INJECTION_SAFE.

PreferenceAction.description: Read, write or clear the stored preferences.

PreviewFormat.description: A previewable artefact: pdf, html or png.

RenderFormat.description: A render target: pdf or html.

RenderScope.description: How much of the folio to render.

RepoFullName.description: A forge repository's full name, owner/name

RepoPath.description: A path relative to the repository root. No `..` segments.

validationRules.description: Specific validation rule IDs to run (empty = all applicable).

stagingLinks.description: The staging preview of the work under review, as the request for feedback carried it, so the reviewer opens the changed pages rather than rebuilding links. Rule: cat-harness skills/authoring/content-lifecycle/feedback-deep-links.md.

skill.content-validate.input.stagingLink.title: Staging links
skill.content-validate.input.stagingLink.description: The staging preview of the work a request for feedback is about: one deep link per changed page (the page and the anchor where the change sits) with the same page on main as `before`. Mirrors StagingComparison in schemas/sdlc/staging.ts. The rule is skills/authoring/content-lifecycle/feedback-deep-links.md. Copied inline as `definitions.stagingLinks` into every skill contract that carries it; schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.

slug.description: Branch slug used in the staging URL path.

pages.description: One entry per changed page, deep-linked; from the change's rendered-impact list, never chosen by judgement.

before.description: Same page on main; absent for a new page.

after.description: The page on the staging preview, with the anchor where the change sits; absent for a deleted page.

summary.description: What to look at on this page.

missing.description: What could not be linked, said rather than hidden: no preview yet (and when it will exist), no page list computed, or a changed page the publish ref does not hold.

skill.content-validate.input.stagingLink.$comment: Copy of cat-harness schemas/staging-comparison.schema.json; cat-harness schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.

skill.content-validate.output.description: Output schema for content validation results.

skill.staging-review.input.title: Staging Review Input
skill.staging-review.input.description: What the reader wants to look at, in their own words (kept verbatim; it narrows, never adds), and the branch or pull request whose preview to list.

ask.description: What the reader wants to look at, verbatim. Absent: the whole preview, every page the branch changed.

skill.staging-review.output.title: Staging Review Output
skill.staging-review.output.description: The reviewable list: a narrative of what changed, where to start, and the staging links, one deep link per changed page with its before. Every other skill that asks for feedback carries this same `stagingLinks` shape.

narrative.description: What a reader of the site will now see or do differently, and why, before any link.

startHere.description: The one page to open first.
